The hall at the Veldmarsh Commercial Vehicle Expo smelled of fresh tyre rubber and floor polish when, on 14 March 2025, Corvane Motors quietly set a number on the table. It came in Technical Specification Bulletin CM-E3/07, a document of the sort that rarely draws a crowd.

For years, electric delivery vans in Norveld were judged by a single anxiety: would they last a working day? Operators learned to plan routes around chargers and to distrust brochure figures. Corvane's answer for the E3 is 510 kilometres on a single charge, measured under a WLTC-style combined test cycle and powered by a 92 kWh battery pack.

Ingrid Halvorsen-Pell, Head of Vehicle Certification at the Norveld Transport Standards Authority, has long argued that such claims matter only when the test method is stated plainly. Here, it is.
